title: Self-Supervised Learning for Graph Dataset Condensation

problem.claim: Graph dataset condensation aims to reduce graph datasets while maintaining model training accuracy, storage cost, and training time.

gap.claim: Existing graph dataset condensation methods are supervised and require massive graph labels, although labels can be scarce in practice.

contributions.claim: SGDC is a self-supervised graph dataset condensation method that does not require label information.
SGDC uses representation matching with target representations from a pre-trained self-supervised learning model to avoid data augmentation and biased gradients.
SGDC combines a graph attention kernel with self-supervised kernel ridge regression and reuses original graph topologies for condensed graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On seven graph datasets, SGDC improves model accuracy by up to 9.7% compared with five state-of-the-art baselines, including baselines that use label information.
SGDC is reported to be significantly more efficient than the baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph dataset condensation reduces graph datasets while preserving training accuracy and improving storage and training efficiency.
Existing methods are supervised and depend on abundant graph labels, which may be scarce.
The proposed self-supervised method begins with bilevel optimization and contrastive learning, but data augmentation causes biased gradient estimation and poor accuracy.
Representation matching removes the need for data augmentation, while a graph attention kernel and adjacency matrix reuse improve efficiency and robustness.
The authors report accuracy gains of up to 9.7% and greater efficiency than five baselines across seven graph datasets.

source_observation.claim: Removing data augmentation through representation matching is presented as a way to avoid biased gradient estimation.

interpretation.claim: When augmentation introduces optimization bias, matching learned representations may provide an alternative training signal.

application.claim: Consider representation-level matching when designing self-supervised condensation or optimization procedures affected by augmentation-induced bias.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether representation matching is effective beyond the reported graph condensation setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the seven datasets, baseline identities, experimental settings, or statistical details.
The abstract does not quantify the reported efficiency improvements or describe the pre-trained self-supervised model.
The abstract does not provide full algorithmic, theoretical, or reproducibility details.
